holidays.name: National Pink Flamingo Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the loud, leggy, gloriously tacky plastic bird that has been stabbed into lawns for decades. Plant a flock in your yard, wear pink, and embrace some kitsch.
holidays.origin: The day commemorates the plastic lawn flamingo designed by artist Don Featherstone in 1957. The bird quickly became a symbol of Americana, especially in Florida.
holidays.funFact: Don Featherstone won the Ig Nobel Prize for art in 1996 for his contribution to the world of kitsch. He reportedly wore matching pink flamingo outfits with his wife.

holidays.name: National Typewriter Day
holidays.description: A click-clack salute to the machine that made writing loud and dramatic. Dust off a vintage model, bang out a letter, and enjoy a keyboard that has no delete key.
holidays.origin: The day marks the typewriter patent granted on June 23, 1868, to Christopher Latham Sholes and his collaborators, who developed the first commercially practical typewriter.
holidays.funFact: The QWERTY layout is commonly linked to Sholes's design. It is often said to have helped keep typebars from jamming, and it still sits under our fingers today.

holidays.name: National Runners Selfie Day
holidays.description: A day for runners to snap a sweaty, triumphant selfie mid-jog or post-run. Flushed cheeks and wild hair are welcome.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, modern social media observance of unclear origin, popular among running fans who share their workouts online.
holidays.funFact: Its hashtag-friendly nature makes it a natural fit for race-day photos. Runners often share selfies with the tag #RunnersSelfieDay.
